column1: # Phase B round ledger — which axis each round advanced.
# Why this file exists (R1526). `tools/phase_b_tally.py` measures an axis by
# COUNTING artifacts, so it can only register work that CREATES one. Depth work
# modifies what already exists: R1523, R1524 and R1525 each closed a named gap
# in the Model/View contract by editing `hello-grid-*` examples the axis already
# owned, and the axis's evidence moved by +0%, +0%, +0%. R1520 and R1521 had
# done the same to the performance axis two rounds earlier. R1522 fixed that one
# by giving perf a `demo-body` probe, which worked only because an optimisation
# happens to leave a NEW demo behind — the cardinality blindness underneath was
# untouched, and it resurfaced on the next axis three rounds later.
# R1522 also recorded why the tool cannot infer this: "a demo is named for the
# round it served and EVERY round has one whatever axis it advanced, so which
# axis owns this demo is frequently unanswerable". Unanswerable BY INFERENCE.
# The round knows. So the round declares it here, and the tally counts
# declarations instead of guessing — the same move as [[r1499]] decoration,
# [[r1501]] surface domain and [[r1517]] focus source.
# Measured before choosing this shape: attributing rounds to axes from git paths
# instead was tried and rejected. R1511 (declared border) and R1513 (dead focus
# half) each touched ~40 examples spanning six axes, so path inference registers
# a sweep round on every axis at once — and unlike a stable false positive in a
# COUNT, which cancels between snapshot and today, that noise ACCUMULATES in a
# rate. Total example bytes was tried too and rejected: it makes verbosity read
# as progress, which the R661 LOC baseline exists to prevent.
# A declaration can be forgotten, which would be the fatal direction (R1522:
# "a false negative on new work is fatal, a false positive cancels"). So git —
# not this file — enumerates which rounds exist, and a round with no row here is
# reported as UNDECLARED at every push. Forgetting is visible, not silent.
# `none` is a legal declaration and needs a reason, for the same reason
# NOT_PHASE_B entries carry one: a documented exclusion can be argued with, a
# silent one cannot.
# Rounds at or below R1519 cannot be declared — the tally was born in R1519 and
# assigning axes to the 1500 rounds before it would be inventing history rather
# than recording it. The floor is stated in the tool and printed in the report.
# Format: round<TAB>axis<TAB>note. Axis is a key from AXES, or `none`.
# round
